edges.mechanism: NAC donates sulfhydryl groups and potentiates nitroglycerin vasodilation (S-nitroso-NAC); symptomatic hypotension 7/24 vs 0/22 with IV NTG + IV NAC.
edges.evidence: Double-blind RCT in unstable angina plus human coronary physiology study, all with IV NAC at doses far above 1.2 g oral; relevance to supplement dose uncertain

edges.mechanism: Ginger reported to potentiate warfarin; turmeric associated with bleeding in anticoagulated patients; curcumin antiplatelet/anticoagulant activity preclinically.
edges.evidence: Evidence reviews and SR of case reports; controlled studies (ginger crossover n=12; Meriva 10-day) found no INR change; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Theoretical additive antiplatelet effect of curcumin and ginger with aspirin/clopidogrel.
edges.evidence: Meriva curcumin did not change bleeding time on aspirin/clopidogrel/ticlopidine over 10 days; 2 g dried ginger had no platelet effect; mechanistic reviews

edges.mechanism: Curcumin inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro and piperine inhibits CYP3A4/P-gp; case of tacrolimus trough 29.9 ng/mL with acute nephrotoxicity after high-dose turmeric.
edges.evidence: Single case report plus in vitro data; very low certainty

edges.with: CYP3A4/CYP2C9 substrates with narrow therapeutic index
edges.mechanism: Curcumin inhibits CYP2C9 (IC50 4.3 uM) and CYP3A4 (IC50 16.3 uM) in vitro; piperine (if present) inhibits CYP3A4, P-gp and glucuronidation.
edges.evidence: In vitro and review evidence; low systemic curcumin exposure limits hepatic relevance

edges.mechanism: Curcumin (FBG -11.48 mg/dL, HbA1c -0.54%) and ginger (FBG -16.27 mg/dL) lower glycemia in T2DM; additive lowering possible.
edges.evidence: RCT meta-analyses; 10-day study found no Meriva-metformin interaction

edges.mechanism: Possible additive glucose lowering from curcumin and ginger.
edges.evidence: 10-day non-interaction study with metformin; MA evidence of glycemic effects; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Charcoal adsorbs acetylcysteine in vitro; NAC reduces charcoal adsorption of acetaminophen and salicylate in vitro.
edges.evidence: Label statement, in vitro data; small human study (n=3) found no significant reduction in NAC absorption

edges.mechanism: Idiosyncratic turmeric/curcumin liver injury; most published cases involved concomitant medications.
edges.evidence: Case series and USP review; no interaction study

edges.mechanism: Duplicate NAC; stacking raises total dose, and NAC side effects appear to increase with dose.
edges.evidence: Sport SR/MA (side-effect OR 1.11) with dose sub-analysis

edges.mechanism: Duplicate curcuminoids; liver injury reported with high-dose, high-bioavailability turmeric products.
edges.evidence: Phytovigilance series and DILIN series

edges.mechanism: Duplicate curcumin; cumulative dose and enhanced formulations increase exposure linked to hepatotoxicity.
edges.evidence: Case series and USP review

edges.mechanism: Duplicate ginger; higher total dose adds GI adverse effects (OA dropouts RR 2.33) and theoretical bleeding effect.
edges.evidence: Meta-analysis and reviews

edges.mechanism: Stacking two botanicals on the US hepatotoxic-botanical list; green tea extract carries its own USP liver caution.
edges.evidence: NHANES exposure study and USP review; no combined-use study

edges.mechanism: Stacking two botanicals among the 6 most-reported hepatotoxic botanicals in the US.
edges.evidence: NHANES exposure study; no combined-use study

edges.mechanism: Garlic strongly associated with surgical bleeding; turmeric linked to bleeding with anticoagulants; additive bleeding risk plausible.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of bleeding risk; no combination study

edges.mechanism: Omega-3s did not raise overall bleeding (RR 1.09), except a small rise with high-dose purified EPA; theoretical additive effect with ginger/curcumin.
edges.evidence: MA of 11 RCTs (n=120,643); review

edges.with: chronic liver disease or prior herb-induced liver injury
edges.mechanism: Turmeric/curcumin liver injury (fatal case in DILIN); more severe recurrence on rechallenge; USP advises consulting a clinician if liver history.
edges.evidence: DILIN, case series, case report, USP review

edges.mechanism: NCCIH states turmeric supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy; ginger alone has supportive trial data; no data on the combination.
edges.evidence: Agency fact sheet; MA of ginger in pregnancy (12 RCTs)

edges.mechanism: Possible antiplatelet effects; review advises stopping nonessential supplements 2 weeks before surgery.
edges.evidence: Narrative review

edges.mechanism: Allele frequency 0.450 in turmeric DILI cases vs 0.056-0.069 in controls; suggests immune-mediated susceptibility.
edges.evidence: DILIN case series (n=10); USP review notes emerging genetic susceptibility

edges.mechanism: In IPF, NAC benefited TT genotype (HR 0.14) but trended toward harm in CC (HR 3.23).
edges.evidence: Post hoc PANTHER-IPF analysis with replication; prospective PRECISIONS trial ongoing

edges.mechanism: NAC falsely lowers creatinine (larger with non-Jaffe/enzymatic methods and IV NAC) without changing cystatin C.
edges.evidence: SR/MA of 6 studies (n=199); in vitro Trinder study

edges.with: Trinder-based assays (triglycerides, cholesterol, uric acid, HDL-C)
edges.mechanism: NAC inhibits peroxidase-coupled Trinder reactions at >=570 mg/L, above expected therapeutic concentrations.
edges.evidence: In vitro analytical study with chart review
